headline: Energy and Chips Lead a Lopsided Tuesday as Consumer Names Bear the Brunt
body_html:
Tuesday's session closed with a pronounced split across the tape, as declining issues outnumbered advancers 325 to 219 out of 545 names tracked — a lopsided result that masked pockets of genuine strength. Energy was the clear sector winner, finishing up 2.2%, aided by reports that a key Saudi Arabian oil pipeline is expected to return to service within days, a development that injected confidence into crude-related names. Semiconductors followed with a 1.08% gain, while Healthcare barely held positive ground at 0.03%. Everything else finished in the red.

The standout mover of the day was Skyworks Solutions, which surged 13.55% to lead all gainers in the universe. Qorvo added 9.34%, giving the RF and semiconductor space an unmistakable bid. Revvity climbed 9.11% in life-science tools, while Valaris tacked on 8.56% as offshore drilling names caught a tailwind from the improving oil-supply picture. On the other side of the ledger, consumer retail absorbed the sharpest punishment: Boot Barn shed 10.13% and Academy Sports dropped 7.02%, with National Vision falling 9.48% in optical retail.

Software declined 1.22% and Consumer fell 1.42% — the two worst sectors on the day — suggesting that rotation out of discretionary and growth-adjacent names accelerated into the close. With geopolitical tensions in the Middle East still unsettled and the Federal Reserve's rate path a live debate among strategists, Tuesday's session offered a reminder that the market's internal architecture can diverge sharply from any headline index reading.

briefs.headline: Saudi Pipeline Recovery Lifts Energy Sentiment
briefs.body: Reports that a major Saudi Arabian oil pipeline could resume operations within days gave energy-sector traders reason to buy on Tuesday. Offshore driller Valaris gained 8.56%, and broader energy names led all sectors with a 2.2% advance. The development offered relief against a backdrop of elevated geopolitical tension across the Middle East.

briefs.headline: RF Chip Makers Stage an Outsized Rally
briefs.body: Skyworks Solutions and Qorvo surged 13.55% and 9.34%, respectively, pulling the semiconductor sector to a 1.08% gain even as much of the market struggled. The paired move pointed to a catalyst specific to the radio-frequency chip space, and the gains rippled into the broader semis group, making it Tuesday's second-best performing sector.

briefs.headline: Consumer Retail Takes the Day's Hardest Hits
briefs.body: Boot Barn plunged 10.13% and Academy Sports slid 7.02%, dragging the consumer sector to a 1.42% loss — the worst on the day. National Vision fell 9.48% in optical retail. The breadth of selling across consumer names suggested sector-wide pressure rather than isolated stock-specific news.

briefs.headline: Treasury Secretary Defends Administration's Economic Stance
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly defended current economic policies and disclosed plans for an upcoming meeting with a Chinese counterpart. The announcement signaled continued high-level trade diplomacy between Washington and Beijing, a development that analysts said could carry implications for supply-chain-sensitive industries in coming weeks.

briefs.headline: Iran War Costs Climb, Adding to Geopolitical Overhang
briefs.body: A Congressional Budget Office assessment pegged the cost of the Iran conflict at 38 billion dollars, with projections calling for an additional three billion dollars per month going forward. The figures added to investor unease already evident in Gulf markets, where most bourses finished in the red amid Houthi activity and disruption to Hormuz shipping lanes.

briefs.headline: Rate Uncertainty Keeps Strategists on Edge
briefs.body: Market professionals continued to debate the implications of a prolonged higher-rate environment for equities and fixed income, with the Federal Reserve's next move still unsettled. Tuesday's session — where software fell 1.22% and consumer declined 1.42% — illustrated how rate-sensitive growth and discretionary segments remain vulnerable when the rate outlook is in flux.
